name: Liberian Cassava Leaf
description: Cassava leaf is a beloved Liberian staple, real technique cooking real ground crayfish and peanut butter together with the leaves until the mixture cooks down nearly dry, before adding the palm oil at the end - this specific order and the crayfish-and-peanut-butter pairing together is genuinely Liberian and Sierra Leonean style, distinct from versions elsewhere that use only one or the other. Real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder, less fibrous approximation.

name: Liberian Palm Butter
description: Palm butter, a rich, oil-forward stew, is a beloved Liberian dish - real palm butter is made from real palm fruit itself, simmered and pounded to extract its oil and pulp, which is genuinely different from just cooking with palm oil; peanut butter and extra palm oil stand in here as the closest approximation, missing the real fruit's distinct thick, fruity body.

Simmer 25-28 minutes until the chicken is very tender and the sauce has thickened into a rich, oil-forward stew.

name: Liberian Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava pounded into a smooth, stretchy dough, is one of Liberia's most essential staples, traditionally torn by hand to scoop up palm butter or cassava leaf.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Drain and pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy, free of lumps.
